title: Managing the Strategy Development Process
coreMove: Build a strategy process that can absorb market learning rather than filtering it out — set direction and limits, then let real evidence change what needs to change.
sourcePressure: Strategy in disruptive settings must be treated as a development process, not a fixed initial design. If the strategy hardens before critical market learning arrives, the plan filters out the evidence that should reshape it. Rigor is still required — but it cannot mean rigid fidelity to the first plan under conditions where important lessons only arrive during action.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Reading this chapter as permission to drift or abandon strategic commitments, when the argument is that leaders must guide strategy seriously while allowing the process to absorb real evidence — not as a concession but as a discipline.

hook: generic 'strategy is dead, execution is everything' framing
generic 'plans are useless, planning is essential' framing
examples: any scene that equates strategy revision with failure
any scene that celebrates a pivot without showing what the learning was that drove it

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: Strategy-process examples should show the moment when evidence arrives and the choice is made about whether to absorb or filter it.

exampleSpecs.domain: health tech startup discovering mid-clinical trial that the primary endpoint is performing but a secondary use case is generating more physician interest
exampleSpecs.audience: a CEO whose board has approved a strategy built entirely around the primary endpoint indication
exampleSpecs.stakes: the secondary use case isn't in the approved strategy, the board presentation, or the regulatory pathway — but physicians in the trial are raising it unsolicited
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Beth has to decide whether to document the secondary use case formally — which would require going back to the board with a strategy revision — or to continue the primary strategy and treat the physician interest as a future option. The moment is about whether the strategy process has a mechanism for absorbing the signal.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a clinical trial dashboard with the primary endpoint meeting target and physician feedback notes about a secondary use case attached at the bottom
mustInclude: the choice of whether to document or filter it
mustAvoid: suggesting that mid-trial pivots are standard clinical practice

exampleSpecs.domain: craft brewery discovering during a new regional distribution expansion that a different product than the flagship is generating the most repeat orders
exampleSpecs.audience: a founder-CEO whose distribution expansion strategy was built around the flagship lager
exampleSpecs.stakes: the expansion plan, marketing spend, and distributor relationships all support the flagship — but reorder data from the new territory shows a seasonal ale outperforming it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Luke's reorder data from week six of the expansion doesn't match the strategy. The seasonal ale wasn't supposed to lead. His distribution plan, marketing commitment, and distributor conversations are all built around the flagship. He has to decide what the data is telling him and whether the strategy process can hold it.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a reorder spreadsheet from a new regional distributor with the seasonal ale in the top row and the flagship in fourth
mustInclude: seasonal ale as the unexpected reorder leader
the strategy process as the mechanism for holding or ignoring the signal
mustAvoid: treating craft brewery as a stand-in for startup culture generally

exampleSpecs.domain: regional airline rerouting when demand data from a new market shows different origin-destination pairs than the strategy modeled
exampleSpecs.audience: a network planning director whose approved route expansion was based on origin-destination demand models built before market entry
exampleSpecs.stakes: the approved routes are not producing the load factors the model predicted, and passenger booking data shows a demand corridor the model missed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Mathieu has to decide whether to adjust the route network based on six weeks of real booking data — which contradicts the model — or to hold the approved strategy through the first full season. The decision is about whether the strategy process has a mechanism for letting real evidence revise the plan.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a network map with approved routes in solid lines and an observed demand corridor in a dotted line not currently served
mustInclude: the choice between holding and revising
mustAvoid: implying that demand modeling is generally unreliable

exampleSpecs.domain: climate-focused VC discovering mid-portfolio review that a grid-storage investment is generating unexpected interest from industrial operators outside the target market
exampleSpecs.audience: a managing partner whose fund thesis is built around utility-scale renewable energy storage
exampleSpecs.stakes: the industrial operators are not in the fund thesis, not in the LP reporting metrics, and not in the investment committee's mental model — but they represent a real demand signal from outside the original target market
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Catarina predicts the industrial operator interest is an edge case that will not produce a fundable market at the fund's check size. The reveal: eighteen months later, industrial storage has attracted two dedicated sector funds and the grid-storage company is generating revenue from industrial clients that the VC's original model did not model.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a portfolio company CRM showing industrial operator inbound inquiries filed under 'out-of-scope leads'
mustInclude: the two dedicated funds in the reveal
mustAvoid: implying that VC fund theses should constantly be revised

exampleSpecs.domain: social enterprise in microfinance discovering that its urban borrowers are using loans differently than the rural model they were trained on
exampleSpecs.audience: a program director whose impact reporting and lending methodology were both designed for rural smallholder borrowers
exampleSpecs.stakes: urban borrowers are using loans for inventory cycles, sub-contracting, and gig-income smoothing — use cases the rural methodology doesn't recognize as on-model, but which are financially real
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Niklas's postmortem on the urban pilot shows that off-model loan uses were flagged for follow-up rather than studied. The methodology treated unfamiliar use as a compliance risk rather than a discovery signal. The strategy process had no mechanism for the urban context to teach the organization anything.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a loan use classification report with urban borrower uses in a grey 'non-standard' category
mustInclude: rural methodology as the strategy anchor
no mechanism for learning in the postmortem finding
mustAvoid: suggesting that rural microfinance methodology is irrelevant to urban lending

exampleSpecs.domain: edtech platform broadening from K-12 to adult learners and discovering that adult engagement patterns require revising the content architecture
exampleSpecs.audience: a product director whose K-12 learning architecture was designed for curriculum-aligned, teacher-assigned content
exampleSpecs.stakes: adult learners are self-directed, skip non-relevant modules, set their own completion timelines, and disengage when content feels school-like — all behaviors the K-12 architecture did not design for
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Before: Adaeze launches the adult learner product using the K-12 platform architecture, because it is proven and the content library already exists. After: three months of engagement data show module abandonment at three times the K-12 rate, self-directed path creation at four times what the architecture was built to support. The after shows the strategy process either learning from the data or not.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an engagement dashboard with K-12 module completion rates in green and adult learner module abandonment in red
mustInclude: K-12 architecture as the strategy anchor
the strategy process choice in the after
mustAvoid: treating adult learners as a less important market than K-12 students

skillTargets: identify when a strategy process is filtering evidence rather than absorbing it
distinguish deliberate strategy revision from undisciplined drift
recognize what a learning signal looks like in a non-technology organizational context
apply emergent-strategy reasoning to a described strategic decision point
evaluate whether a described strategy process has a mechanism for revision

tryThisNowSpec: Think of the last time your organization received information that contradicted the current plan. Write down whether that information was absorbed into the strategy or filed as an exception. Name one change to your review process that would make the next signal harder to file away.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one direct second-person paragraph asking the reader to name the last piece of evidence that their strategy process turned into an exception
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
